title: Uniform smooth-span lifting on principal singularity fibres
statement: Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. A principal singularity pair $(X,I)$ means an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an ideal $I=(\pi)$ with $\pi$ a non-zero-divisor, and $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(I)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Write $X_m=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^m)$ and $I_m=I\mathcal O_{X_m}$. Maps of pairs preserve the distinguished ideals by extension. There exists an integer $r\geq0$ depending only on $(X,I)$ with the following uniform property. Let $u:(X',I')\to(X,I)$ be any smooth $k$-morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with $(X',I')$ another principal singularity pair (the identity is allowed). Let $(Y,J)$ be any principal singularity pair over $k$, let $m>r$, and let $a:(Y_{m+r},J_{m+r})\to(X'_{m+r},I'_{m+r})$ be smooth over $k$. There are a finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$, an ideal $K=J\mathcal O_Z$, an etale map $g:Z\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing isomorphisms $Z_t\simeq Y_t$ for every $t\geq1$, and a smooth map $f:Z\to X'$ preserving the distinguished ideals, such that $a|_m=f_m\circ g_m^{-1}$. The bound $r$ is independent of $u$, $Y$, $m$, and $a$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.2, Proposition 3.3.1, Remark 3.2.2(i)--(ii) and definition of conductor in 3.2.5; uniform version for smooth targets; printed pp.20--22; read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this specialized assertion.

proof.text: Choose a generator $\pi$ of $I$. Apply [lem-per-principal-parameter-conductor-bound] to obtain $q(0)\ne0$ and $r\ge1$. Write $A_*=A[1/q(\pi)]$. For every smooth $u$, its base change $X'_*\to\operatorname{Spec}A_*$ is smooth: an affine first-order lifting problem over $X'_*$ is the same problem over $X'$ together with the fixed base map, so the definition supplies a lift. Hence [lem-per-gabber-ramero-ideal-calculus] gives $\pi^r\in H_{A'_*/k[t]}$, where $A'_*=\mathcal O(X')[1/q(u^*\pi)]$. This fixes $r$ before $u,Y,m,a$ are chosen. The open contains the whole distinguished fibre.

Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $J=(s)$ and $N=m+r$. The image of $u^*\pi$ under $a^*$ generates $J/J^N$; lift it to $\rho=sv\in J$. Then $(s)=(sv)+(s^N)$ gives $1=vw+s^{N-1}c$ by cancelling the non-zero-divisor $s$. Thus $v$ is a unit on a neighbourhood of $V(J)$. Replace $Y$ by $D(v)$, which contains every $Y_t$; now $J=(\rho)$ and $\rho$ is a non-zero-divisor. Also $q(\rho)$ is a unit modulo every $J^t$, since its constant term is nonzero. Consequently $a$ factors through $X'_{*,N}$. Give $B$ the $k[t]$-structure $t\mapsto\rho$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, choice of the lifted parameter

proof.text: Form $H=B^h$ for $(B,J)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. It is henselian, Noetherian, flat over $B$, and has the same quotients modulo $J^t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion] and [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-flat-quotients]. Thus $\rho$ is a non-zero-divisor on $H$ by the defining tensor test for flatness. The finite-type algebras $A'_*,B$ are Noetherian and finitely presented over their Noetherian bases by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. The smooth map $A_*\to A'_*$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]; $A_*$ is flat over $k[t]$ by Step 1. Flat transitivity and base change give $C=A'_*\otimes_{k[t]}H$ flat over $H$, using [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. In particular $\rho$ is a non-zero-divisor on $C$. By [lem-per-gabber-ramero-ideal-calculus], $\rho^r\in H_{C/H}$. The map $a$ defines the $H$-algebra retraction $C/\rho^NC\to H/\rho^NH$, $x\otimes h\mapsto a^*(x)h$. Apply [lem-per-gabber-ramero-henselian-section-lifting] with $n=m>r$ to obtain $C\to H$ agreeing modulo $\rho^m$, hence a $k[t]$-algebra map $A'_*\to H$.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.3 and Proposition 3.3.1 proof, henselian base change

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], $H$ is the filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras $D$ with $B/J\simeq D/JD$. Give each the $k[t]$-structure $t\mapsto\rho$. The finitely presented $k[t]$-algebra $A'_*$ and its map to $H$ therefore descend to a map $A'_*\to D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit]. Put $Z^0=\operatorname{Spec}D$. The map $D\to H$ and $B\to D$ have canonically isomorphic quotients modulo $J^t$: the latter by etale flatness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers], and the former by comparison with $B\to H$. Thus the descended map agrees with $a$ modulo $J^m$ and preserves $J$ exactly, since it sends $u^*\pi$ to $\rho$. The scheme $Z^0$ is finite type over $k$. Since $D$ is finite type over the Noetherian ring $B$, it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. It is finite type over $A'_*$ via this map (a finite list of $k$-algebra generators suffices), hence finitely presented over it by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, finite-presentation descent; Stacks Tags 0A02 and 0AGU

proof.text: The special-fibre map $Z^0_1\to X'_{*,1}$ is the base change of $a|_m$, hence smooth. Base change follows directly from the first-order lifting definition: an affine lifting problem for the pullback is one for $a$ with its prescribed base coordinate. At any $z\in Z^0_1$, put $x=f^0(z)$ and localize $A'_*\to D$ at $x,z$. These are Noetherian local rings; $u^*\pi$ and its image $\rho$ are non-zero-divisors, the latter because $B\to D$ is etale and flat. The quotient local map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-criterion-nonzerodivisor] with module equal to $D_z$, finite over itself, to obtain flatness of the local map. Its fibre at $x$ is the fibre of the smooth special-fibre map, so [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] makes $f^0$ smooth near $z$. Take the union $Z$ of these smooth neighbourhoods. It contains the entire $Z^0_1$, so it contains every infinitesimal fibre $Z^0_t$, whose underlying set is $Z^0_1$. Since $Z^0$ is Noetherian this open is quasi-compact and finite type over $k$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 proof, Cartier local flatness and shrinking; Stacks 00ML and 01V9

proof.text: Restricting the etale map $Z^0\to Y$ to $Z$ and composing with the open immersion $D(v)\hookrightarrow Y$ gives the required etale $g$: at every point of $Z$, source and target can be restricted to the same affine neighbourhoods as for $Z^0\to D(v)$, since the intervening immersions are open. The local affine etale condition is therefore the identical one. Put $K=J\mathcal O_Z$. Both shrinkings contain the whole distinguished fibre, so $g_t$ is still an isomorphism for every $t\ge1$. The descended map $f:Z\to X'_*\hookrightarrow X'$ is smooth by the same open-target local test and satisfies $f^*I'=K$ and $f_m=a|_m\circ g_m$, whence the asserted identity. If $V(J)$ is empty, take $Z=\varnothing$ from the start. If $V(I)$ is empty then $I'=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and existence of the map of pairs $a$ forces $J/J^N=\mathcal O_{Y_N}$; a nilpotent unit ideal forces $Y_N=\varnothing$, so this is the same empty case. The integer $r$ was fixed in Step 1.
